scenario.name: Sigstore Cosign, NIST SP 800-190 & MITRE — OCI Container Registry Layer Tampering & Image Digest Verification Audit
scenario.overview: Imagine an underground city subway metro station with tiled tunnel walls, glowing route maps, chrome fare turnstiles, ticket kiosks, and a gleaming metro train sliding along the platform. Down in the underground subway concourse, a rider taps a replayed magnetic metro fare card at the chrome turnstile bank during evening rush hour. In this real-world scenario, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the metro card turnstile bank in tiny disguised batches, then smuggles copied records out past the metro card turnstile bank in tiny disguised batches. The metro booth attendant’s fare-gate console flags a single card swiped at two distant stations within seconds and alerts transit security. In this scenario (T1525, Sigstore Cosign, NIST SP 800-190 & MITRE, OCI Container Registry Layer Tampering & Image Digest Verification Audit), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: uploading Modified OCI Layer Blob via POST, then overwriting Mutable Image Tag via PUT, then admission Controller Sigstore Cosign. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Uploading Modified OCI Layer Blob via POST, then Overwriting Mutable Image Tag via PUT, then Admission Controller Sigstore Cosign, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates process, authentication, and network telemetry for T1525 across the documented kill chain.

stages.title: Stage 3: Admission Controller Sigstore Cosign Signature Verification & Layer Diff Forensics
stages.subtitle: Initial Access & Execution Prevention (T1525 - Implant Internal Image)
stages.description: Inside the subway cab, the intruder reads the station relay schedule and triggers an unauthorized express skip past the next inspection stop. In this final step inside the subway metro, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the metro card turnstile bank in tiny disguised batches until the fare-gate audit console catches the mismatch. When a Kubernetes Deployment with imagePullPolicy: Always attempts to schedule the updated :prod tag, the Sigstore Policy Controller / Kyverno VerifyImages admission webhook checks the Rekor transparency log and Cosign signature (.sig), blocking the unsigned manifest (logged in Linux Audit Event 403 with AdmissionWebhook=policy.sigstore.dev , Sigstore Cosign / Kyverno, RejectedDigest=sha256:deadbeef8899, EnforcementOutcome=HTTP 403 Forbidden , Unsigned Image Blocked so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes kubectl get events -n prod --field-selector reason=PolicyViolation (which executes a Kubernetes API request or container runtime command , kubectl get events -n prod --field-selector reason=PolicyViolation configuring pod so that breaks out of container cgroup/namespace isolation , T1525 during "Admission Controller Sigstore Cosign Signature Verification & Layer Diff Forensics" to gain unrestricted root execution on the underlying Kubernetes worker node and access host credentials , kubelet / systemd). Next, the follow-up artifact dive registry.corp.local/corp/payment-api@sha256:deadbeef8899 --ci runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , dive registry.corp.local/corp/payment-api@sha256:deadbeef8899 --ci via System / Runtime Exec so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1525 during "Admission Controller Sigstore Cosign Signature Verification & Layer Diff Forensics" , When a Kubernetes Deployment with imagePullPolicy: Always attempts to schedule the updated :prod tag, the Sigstore Policy Controller / Kyverno VerifyImages admission webhook checks the Rekor transparency log and Cosign signature , while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ admission webhook "policy.sigstore.dev" denied request: no matching signatures found for sha256:deadbeef8899 / ⇠#3 ACK 403) from Node ③ (#3 OCI Container Registry (/v2/ API)) to Node ④ (#4 Mutable Tag (:prod Manifest Put)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Kubernetes Node containerd Image Pull).

keySpecs.value: Enforce Sigstore Cosign keyless OIDC signing in CI/CD and deploy Kyverno VerifyImages or Sigstore Policy Controller in Enforcing mode on all Kubernetes clusters.
